source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check system protection when fan status is change
1. Power on system and boot into OS.
2. Run BurnIn test, make system has heavy load.
3. Make Fan 1 can`t work,check other fans speed would rise up.
4. Make Fan 1 to work, check all fan`s speed would back to orginal.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Make sure Fan would change speed when some fan fail
2. Make sure fan would be adjust its speed to orginal when the problem is solved

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: ipmitool + BMC creds + operator (fail a fan)

deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the fan-fault SEL + the fan-speed response so the user confirms the fan-fail protection acted (alarm/ramp).

original_test_intent: Verify that under an approved heavy BurnIn load, loss of Fan 1 makes the remaining fans increase speed and restoration of Fan 1 returns all fans to the defined original automatic-control state.
original_method: The source does not define the essential Fan 1 failure operation. Jamming, unplugging, hot-removal and BMC disabling have different hazards and coverage, particularly under heavy load, so no safe fail/restore sequence can be selected.
manual_activity: If the selected failure requires physical fan manipulation, a qualified operator must perform and reverse it. This cannot be determined until the owner defines the failure path; automated telemetry alone cannot create the required state.
required_inputs: Exact Fan 1 FRU/slot/zone and supported failure mechanism
Tested restoration method and maximum failure interval
Approved BurnIn tool/profile/duration and heavy-load power/thermal envelope
Expected remaining-fan ramp and return-to-original tolerances, abort limits and OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Do not jam, unplug, remove or disable Fan 1 by inference, especially under heavy load.
Do not start BurnIn until the failure/recovery action and continuous safety monitoring are validated.
After unblocking, abort load and restore cooling immediately on temperature, RPM, alarm, service or OOB limit.
Preserve the first fault/recovery sequence; no automatic retry or alternative failure mechanism.
agent_execution_scope: While blocked, prepare only baseline fan/thermal/load/SEL collection and review the proposed method.
After formal approval, run the bounded workload and collect synchronized per-fan ramp/recovery evidence around the operator or approved injector action.
Terminate workloads and report facts without performing undefined physical actions or issuing the verdict.
engineer_actions: Choose and validate the Fan 1 fail/restore mechanism and physical operator requirements.
Define workload, response tolerances and safety limits.
Authorize execution, verify restoration and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its read-only sensor/SEL collection is supporting evidence only. It does not define the source's core fault or BurnIn, and grep filters are inadequate for complete protection evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No failure command or physical method is recommended while blocked. After owner definition, retain the exact approved BurnIn and fail/restore procedure and capture full unfiltered telemetry.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Heavy BurnIn load, Fan 1 failed/restored states, other-fan ramp/return and attended/machine times 20/10 are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Once a platform-supported fault path is chosen, synchronize bounded BurnIn, one Fan 1 transition, all-zone RPM/thermal/event telemetry, restoration and cooldown with deterministic stop controls.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Undetermined until the exact fan architecture and supported failure path are supplied.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record fan FRU, BMC/CPLD, BurnIn and any injector/tool versions after selection.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform fan-fault/service and automatic-control specifications are required.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing operation, quantitative response and recovery boundaries without guessing them.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Different fault mechanisms exercise different detection paths; equivalence cannot be assumed.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Failure/restore method, workload, fan map, tolerances and limits.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A software disable may not emulate mechanical loss; hot removal may be unsupported and jamming may damage the fan.

project_override_considerations: A project may select one documented safe failure path and report only that path's coverage. Until selected, the case remains blocked because the missing input defines the operation itself, not merely a parameter.
expected_evidence: Approved Fan 1 map, failure/restore method, maximum interval and authorization
BurnIn identity/profile/duration, load/power and abort limits
Synchronized all-fan RPM, temperature, threshold, SEL and workload evidence before/fault/recovery
Proven process cleanup, Fan 1 restoration, return-to-baseline and final health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criteria consistently require compensation during Fan 1 failure and return afterward. The issue is omission of the essential fault semantics, not contradictory statements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Making Fan 1 'not work' under heavy load is the core operation, but its mechanism is absent. The available options differ materially in safety and coverage, so guessing would be unsafe and technically invalid.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retain its operator dependency and telemetry role but reject the implied undefined fault as executable.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keep its load, monitoring and recovery requirements; change to BLOCKED until the core fail/restore semantics are chosen.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Applies the narrow blocked rule to a missing necessary operation rather than to ordinary project parameters.

review_improvement: Prevents an unsafe fan fault under heavy load and ensures that any future method has explicit, non-interchangeable coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: The prior passive/obstruction case specified a physical mechanism; this one does not. Under heavy load, choosing among jam, unplug, removal or controller disable changes both hazard and what protection path is tested. That is an unresolved necessary operation, so BLOCKED is justified.
